courts.name: West 4th Street Courts (The Cage)
courts.address: Avenue of the Americas, W 3rd St and W 4th St, New York, NY 10014
courts.courts: Multiple courts; the main caged court is smaller than regulation size
courts.hours: Open to the public; NYC Parks does not publish posted court hours
courts.notable: Known as "The Cage" for the 20-foot chain-link fence that encloses a court about half regulation size. It is home to the West 4th Summer League, the oldest summer basketball program in New York City, and draws players and spectators from outside the neighborhood.
courts.quick_answer: The West 4th Street Courts, known as "The Cage," are a free public outdoor basketball court in Greenwich Village, Manhattan, at Avenue of the Americas between West 3rd and West 4th Streets. The main court is enclosed by a 20-foot chain-link fence and is smaller than regulation size, which puts a premium on physical play.

faqs.q: Is The Cage free to play at?
faqs.a: Yes. West 4th Street Courts is a New York City public park, so access is free. NYC Parks does not publish posted court hours for the site.

faqs.q: Why is it called The Cage?
faqs.a: The main basketball court is enclosed on all sides by a 20-foot-high chain-link fence. The nickname stuck because of the fence and because the court is about half regulation size, which makes play unusually physical.

faqs.q: How big is the court at West 4th Street?
faqs.a: The main caged court is smaller than regulation size. City Lore describes it as roughly half regulation size, and Wikipedia notes the non-regulation size places greater emphasis on inside play.

faqs.q: When is the best time to find a game at The Cage?
faqs.a: The West 4th Summer League plays a game every day of the week in June, July and August, with five games on Saturdays and Sundays. City Lore reports more than 600 players take part each year.

courts.quick_answer: Rucker Park is a free public outdoor basketball court at 280 West 155th Street in Harlem, New York City. It is named for Holcombe Rucker, the playground director who started a citywide youth tournament there in 1950, and it is one of the most widely recognized outdoor courts in the United States.

faqs.q: Where is Rucker Park?
faqs.a: At 280 West 155th Street in Harlem, New York, NY 10039. It is a New York City public park.

faqs.q: Is Rucker Park free?
faqs.a: Yes. Rucker Park is a public New York City park and access to the outdoor courts is free.

faqs.q: Who was Holcombe Rucker?
faqs.a: Holcombe Rucker was a New York City playground director who founded a citywide youth basketball tournament in Harlem in 1950. The park was renamed in his honor.

faqs.q: Can you play at Rucker Park at night?

courts.name: Dyckman Park
courts.address: 4768 Nagle Ave, Inwood, New York, NY
courts.courts: Three courts: Court A (main court), Court B (smaller full court) and Court C (half court)
courts.access: Free, public NYC park; the tournament area runs bag checks during games
courts.hours: Park is public; scoreboard and lights are cut at about 9:35 pm during the summer tournament
courts.surface: Cushioned court surfacing added in a $9.5 million renovation completed in 2023
courts.notable: Known as "The Red Carpet of Streetball." The Dyckman Basketball summer tournament launched in 1990 with two hoops, a court and some paint, and now runs nearly every night through the summer. A $9.5 million parks renovation added cushioned surfacing, permanent steel bleachers and a scoreboard.
courts.quick_answer: Dyckman Park is a free public outdoor basketball complex at 4768 Nagle Avenue in Inwood, Manhattan. It has three courts and hosts the Dyckman Basketball summer tournament, known as "The Red Carpet of Streetball," which plays nearly every night through the summer and has drawn NBA players including Kevin Durant and Kyrie Irving.

faqs.q: How many basketball courts does Dyckman Park have?
faqs.a: Three. Court A is the main court used for high school and adult competition, Court B is a smaller full court, and Court C is a half court that portable baskets convert into a full court for young players.

faqs.q: Is Dyckman Park free to play at?
faqs.a: Yes, it is a New York City public park. During the summer tournament the playing area is barricaded and entry involves a bag check.

faqs.q: Why is Dyckman called The Red Carpet of Streetball?
faqs.a: The nickname dates to 2011, when Nike laid out a literal red carpet at Dyckman for Kevin Durant. The name stuck as the tournament grew into one of the most attended streetball events in the country.

faqs.q: How late can you play at Dyckman Park?
faqs.a: The scoreboard and lights at Dyckman are controlled by the Parks Department and shut off at about 9:35 pm, according to the tournament's chief operating officer.

courts.quick_answer: Fonde Recreation Center is a publicly accessible indoor basketball gym near downtown Houston, Texas, commonly called Fonde. It is known as a summer proving ground for college and NBA players, including Hakeem Olajuwon, Moses Malone and Clyde Drexler, and it remains the home of the Nike Houston Pro City summer league.

faqs.q: Is Fonde Recreation Center indoors or outdoors?
faqs.a: Indoor. Fonde is a public recreation center gymnasium near downtown Houston, not an outdoor court.

faqs.q: Why is Fonde famous?
faqs.a: Fonde is known for its summer basketball, which served as a proving ground for NCAA and NBA players. Among the most cited stories are the early-1980s duels between Moses Malone and Hakeem Olajuwon.

faqs.q: How do you pronounce Fonde?
faqs.a: The gym is pronounced "fon-DEE" and is also commonly called Fonde Rec.

courts.name: Venice Beach Basketball Courts
courts.courts: Four courts: three side by side plus a main court with bleachers
courts.notable: Four asphalt courts on the sand at Venice Beach, adjacent to Muscle Beach. Three courts sit side by side, with one reserved for 5-on-5 play and two for 3-on-3; a separate main court with a blue surface and bleachers hosts the biggest crowds. The courts appeared in White Men Can't Jump and American History X.
courts.quick_answer: The Venice Beach Basketball Courts are four free public outdoor courts at 1708-1798 Ocean Front Walk in Venice, Los Angeles, California. Three courts sit side by side, with one reserved for 5-on-5 and two for 3-on-3, plus a main court with bleachers. The Venice Basketball League has run there since 2006.

faqs.q: How many basketball courts are at Venice Beach?
faqs.a: Four. Three are located side by side, one for 5-on-5 play and two for 3-on-3. A separate main court sits to the north with bleachers for spectators.

faqs.q: Are the Venice Beach basketball courts free?
faqs.a: Yes, they are free and public. Note that the City of Los Angeles has at times cordoned or locked the hoops, so availability can be affected by city policy.

faqs.q: What movies were filmed at the Venice Beach courts?
faqs.a: The courts played a prominent role in the 1992 film White Men Can't Jump and appear in a pivotal basketball scene in American History X.

faqs.q: Is there a league at Venice Beach?
faqs.a: Yes. The Venice Basketball League, also called Veniceball, has run at the courts since 2006, with a twelve-team summer season from early June to mid-August.

faqs.q: Where is Mosswood Park?
